title: Antiatoms
description: An antiproton and a positron make antihydrogen - with exactly the same spectrum as hydrogen. Unlocks the Antiproton Decelerator.

puzzle.goal: An antiproton and a positron are bound by the same Coulomb attraction as a proton and an electron. Treat the two-body problem with the reduced mass of the pair, quantise the angular momentum, and write the energy of the n-th bound level in terms of the masses, the elementary charge, the vacuum permittivity and the Planck constant.
puzzle.name: Bohr levels of (anti)hydrogen with reduced mass
puzzle.ask: CPT symmetry makes antihydrogen's levels identical to hydrogen's: E_n = −R/n² with R = 13.606 eV. Find the photon energy (eV) of the 2 → 1 transition probed by laser spectroscopy.
puzzle.method: Balance the Coulomb force against the centripetal force of the reduced mass, impose L = nħ, then add kinetic and potential energy.
